source: Arc Request for Builders (Team Arc, published 2026-09-16), paraphrased by stable-build contributors
license: Our own paraphrase (MIT). The RFB itself has no license; read it at source_url. Block facts link to docs.arc.io or developers.circle.com.
notes: items[] are the RFB's four frontiers in our words. rfb_start_with lists what the RFB suggests starting with; today.blocks lists what is usable now. blocks[] status: live | permissioned (access must be granted) | testnet-only | roadmap (not available; never a required block). Re-check a block through the arc-docs MCP before relying on it.

items.summary: Dollars, FX and payments built so deep into a product that the user never has to think about how the money moves.

opportunities.name: Local-market finance apps
opportunities.idea: A product for one country, corridor or community that bundles dollar access, FX, savings and payments; local licensing, distribution and UX are the edge.

opportunities.name: Programmable trade workflows
opportunities.idea: Commercial agreements as code: milestone releases, dispute handling and conditional settlement paid in USDC.

opportunities.name: Borderless payroll
opportunities.idea: An employer tool that covers onboarding, local compliance, tax and funding, so paying a team spread across many countries is one routine.

today.note: StableFX is permissioned for vetted institutions; for most builders, FX starts with the App Kit Swap capability.

items.summary: Agents can already hold and spend USDC. Missing: businesses that agents run, markets that pay for agent work, and cover for when agents get it wrong.

opportunities.name: Agent-run businesses
opportunities.idea: A small team of agents with a USDC treasury on Arc that buys the services it needs and settles its own costs onchain, with no staff.

opportunities.name: Outcome marketplaces
opportunities.idea: Post a goal with a USDC bounty; an agent or a person delivers; payment is released only when the result is checked against an agreed standard.

opportunities.name: Cover for agent failures
opportunities.idea: Parametric cover for losses caused by agents moving funds (deposits, swaps, rebalances), with a clear premium schedule and a claims path that pays.
opportunities.caution: Insurance is regulated in most places; this kit gives no legal advice.

today.note: ERC-8183 jobs are documented as a testnet tutorial; mainnet deployment is UNVERIFIED.

items.summary: Putting assets onchain is solved. Lending against them still needs collateral a lender can verify, privacy that still allows disclosure, and risk models institutions accept.

opportunities.name: Collateral APIs
opportunities.idea: A service that lets a brokerage, neobank or consumer app offer USDC credit against assets its users already hold, with the position monitored onchain.

opportunities.name: Long-tail credit markets
opportunities.idea: Credit for fragmented assets such as equipment, trade receivables or royalties, opened to lenders who cannot reach them today.

opportunities.name: Embedded protection
opportunities.idea: Cover for smart-contract or collateral loss built into USDC deposit and lending flows, with coverage data in a standard format.
opportunities.caution: Credit and insurance are regulated activities; this kit gives no legal or financial advice.

today.note: Arc Privacy is on the roadmap and not available. Start with public contracts and the App Kit Borrow capability; keep data that would need privacy offchain for now.

items.summary: Personal money that runs itself: one programmable balance that pays, saves and hands bounded tasks to agents, with the user approving only the exceptions.

opportunities.name: Household finance office
opportunities.idea: One programmable balance for a family's cash, bills, subscriptions and savings, with routine decisions automated and the user stepping in only when needed.

opportunities.name: Themed baskets
opportunities.idea: A single interface over baskets built around a theme or a specialist manager; the user picks the exposure and the app handles the mechanics.
opportunities.caution: Touches regulated investment activity; this kit gives no investment, legal or tax advice.

opportunities.name: Agents with a mandate
opportunities.idea: Agents that act on a user's funds inside hard limits the user sets, using Gateway to reach USDC on other supported chains without moving the agent.
opportunities.caution: Touches regulated investment activity; this kit gives no investment, legal or tax advice.

today.note: All three suggested blocks are live.

blocks.name: USDC on Arc (native gas, 18 decimals; ERC-20 interface, 6 decimals)
blocks.what: One balance with two views. Fees are paid in USDC. Address 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 on both networks.

blocks.name: EURC
blocks.what: Euro stablecoin on Arc, 6 decimals. Mainnet and testnet addresses differ.

blocks.name: App Kits SDK
blocks.what: SDK for Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn and Borrow; all seven are listed for Arc.
blocks.note: Borrow lends USDC against cirBTC. find-idea does not build ideas on Earn: it would invite return claims, which this kit never makes.

blocks.name: Transaction memos (Memo contract)
blocks.what: Attach an app-defined memoId and memo bytes to a contract call such as a USDC transfer; the wallet stays msg.sender.
blocks.note: The direct caller must be an EOA; smart accounts revert. Memo bytes are public.

blocks.name: Batched transactions (Multicall3From)
blocks.what: Batch several calls in one transaction while each subcall keeps the sending wallet as msg.sender.
blocks.note: EOA only; no value forwarding (no aggregate3Value).

blocks.name: CCTP (Arc is domain 26)
blocks.what: Move USDC and EURC between Arc and other chains by burn and mint.
blocks.note: Sends to Stellar (domain 27) must route through CctpForwarder: https://developers.circle.com/cctp/references/stellar

blocks.name: Circle Gateway
blocks.what: A unified USDC balance usable across supported chains; GatewayWallet and GatewayMinter are deployed on Arc.

blocks.name: Gateway Nanopayments (x402)
blocks.what: Gas-free, batched sub-cent USDC payments, for example pay-per-request APIs for agents.
blocks.note: Supported on the EVM chains in Gateway's list; Arc is included through Gateway's Arc deployment.

blocks.name: Circle Agent Stack (Circle CLI, agent wallets, agent nanopayments)
blocks.what: Tooling for agents to hold USDC, pay for services and transact with spending controls. Agent Wallets list Arc on mainnet and testnet.

blocks.name: Circle Wallets (developer-controlled, user-controlled, modular)
blocks.what: Embedded wallets; Arc is supported for EOA and smart-contract account types.
blocks.note: Memo and Multicall3From need an EOA caller.

blocks.name: Gasless USDC transfers through an EIP-3009 relayer
blocks.what: Collect a transferWithAuthorization signature and broadcast it from your own funded relayer EOA.

blocks.name: Self-deployed ERC-4337 paymaster
blocks.what: Sponsor user operations; the EntryPoint deposit is funded in native USDC (18 decimals).

blocks.name: ERC-8004 agent identity, reputation and validation registries
blocks.what: Registries deployed on Arc mainnet and testnet for agent identity and reputation.

blocks.name: ERC-8183 jobs with USDC escrow
blocks.what: Create a job, fund escrow in USDC, submit a deliverable hash and settle. Documented as an Arc Testnet tutorial.
blocks.note: No mainnet address on the contract addresses page on 2026-10-04 (UNVERIFIED for mainnet).

blocks.name: StableFX
blocks.what: Institutional stablecoin FX engine with escrow settlement on Arc (FxEscrow).
blocks.note: Access is for vetted institutions. Most builders should start FX with App Kit Swap.

blocks.name: Arc Privacy Sector (opt-in private execution)
blocks.what: Planned confidential execution for Solidity contracts alongside the public EVM.
blocks.note: The docs say privacy features are on the roadmap and not yet available. Never make it a required block.
